en: to be numerous; to be abundant; to be copious

examples.en: I met countless people on that road.
That actor has won awards countless times.
I had countless failures, but I didn't give up.
There were countless rumors about that singer.

examples.ko: 이 일을 하며 겪은 고생이 숱해서 말로 다 못 해요.
examples.en: I've been through so many hardships in this job that I can't put them all into words.
My many worries disappeared one by one.

explain: '많다'보다 글 같은 느낌이고, '숱한 실패', '숱한 밤'처럼 지나온 경험이나 사례가 아주 많다고 돌아볼 때 잘 어울려요. '숱하게 + 동사' 모양도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: He succeeded after countless failures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나온 경험이 아주 많았다고 돌아볼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when looking back on very many past experiences.

phrases.en: I have heard that story countless times.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숱하게'는 동사 앞에서 횟수가 아주 많다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 숱하게 before a verb adds the sense of very many times.

phrases.en: There were many people I met on that road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숱하다'보다 일상적이고 가벼운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual and plain word than 숱하다.

explain_en: It feels more literary than '많다' and fits when looking back on very many experiences or cases, as in '숱한 실패' or '숱한 밤'. The '숱하게 + verb' pattern is also common.

examples.en: I am a longtime devoted reader of this magazine.
I would like to thank all our devoted readers.

examples.ko: 애독자 엽서를 보내면 선물을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you send in a reader postcard, you can get a gift.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 애독자라서 신간을 바로 샀어요.
examples.en: I'm a devoted fan of that author, so I bought the new book right away.
As the novel became popular, its loyal readers increased.
Devoted readers sent many letters to the author.

explain: 책, 신문, 잡지를 좋아해서 꾸준히 읽는 사람을 말해서, 그냥 '독자'보다 애정이 느껴져요. 신문이나 잡지에서 '애독자 여러분'이라고 인사하는 말이 자주 나와요. '그 작가의 애독자'처럼 특정 작가나 책에도 써요.

phrases.en: Dear readers, thank you again today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡지나 신문에서 독자에게 인사할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A greeting to readers used in magazines and newspapers.

phrases.en: I am a devoted reader of that comic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특정 작품을 좋아하는 독자를 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a reader who loves a particular work.
phrases.en_equiv: a fan reader of that comic

phrases.example: 한 번 읽고 나서 애독자가 됐어요.
phrases.en: After reading it once, I became a devoted reader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋아서 계속 읽게 된 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes becoming a loyal reader after liking something.

explain_en: It refers to someone who loves a book, newspaper or magazine and reads it regularly, so it feels warmer than plain '독자'. Newspapers and magazines often greet readers with '애독자 여러분'. It can also be used for a particular author or book, as in '그 작가의 애독자'.

t90.ax: I would like to thank all our devoted readers.

examples.en: She is called a heroine of the political world.
I read stories about heroic women in history.
The heroine of that movie is a bold, spirited woman.
My grandmother was known as a strong woman in the village.

examples.ko: 여걸 소리를 들을 만큼 배짱이 있어요.
examples.en: She has enough nerve to be called a heroine.
One heroic woman appears in the novel.

explain: 배짱과 능력이 뛰어나서 남자 못지않다는 칭찬으로 쓰는 말이에요. 주로 글이나 이야기에서 만나고, 보통 '여걸로 불리다', '여걸 소리를 듣다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 그분은 젊을 때부터 여걸 소리를 들었어요.
phrases.en: She has been called a heroine since she was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변에서 여걸이라고 부른다는 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means people around her call her a heroine.

phrases.en: Her calm in a crisis is truly worthy of a heroine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-답다'를 붙여 여걸에 어울리는 모습을 칭찬해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-답다' praises someone for acting worthy of a heroine.

phrases.en: My grandmother is a well-known strong woman in the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여걸'과 비슷하게 배짱 있고 씩씩한 여성을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like '여걸', it refers to a bold, spirited woman.

explain_en: It is praise for a woman with great nerve and ability, as capable as any man. You mostly meet it in writing and stories, usually in patterns like '여걸로 불리다' or '여걸 소리를 듣다'.

t90.ax: One heroic woman appears in the novel.

examples.en: The flowers are blooming in little clusters.

examples.ko: 아이들이 올망졸망 줄을 서서 버스를 기다려요.
examples.en: The little kids are lined up in a row, waiting for the bus.

examples.ko: 작은 집들이 올망졸망 붙어 있는 골목이에요.
examples.en: It's an alley where small houses sit snugly together.
The chicks sitting close together are so cute.

examples.ko: 가방 속에 올망졸망 담긴 과자들을 꺼냈어요.
examples.en: I took out the small snacks packed together in my bag.

examples.ko: 올망졸망 모여 있는 섬들을 배 위에서 바라봤어요.
examples.en: I looked from the boat at the small islands clustered together.

explain: 작고 비슷한 것들이 여럿 모여 있는 모습이에요. 아이, 꽃, 집처럼 귀엽고 정겨운 느낌이 있는 것에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The flowerpots in the yard are clustered together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'를 붙여 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 describes a state.

phrases.en: The children sat together in a little cluster.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 아이들이 모인 모습에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits the image of small children gathered together.

phrases.en: I can see little houses clustered at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 정겨운 집들을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for small, cozy-looking houses.

explain_en: It describes many small, similar things gathered together. It suits things with a cute, homey feel, such as children, flowers and houses.

t90.ax: The flowers are blooming in little clusters.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 조선 왕가의 이야기를 다뤄요.
examples.en: This drama deals with the story of the Joseon royal family.
I watched the British royal family's wedding on TV.

examples.ko: 왕가의 일원으로 태어나면 자유롭게 살기 어려워요.
examples.en: If you're born into a royal family, it's hard to live freely.

examples.ko: 왕가 사람들이 쓰던 그릇을 박물관에서 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw bowls used by royal family members at the museum.
The two royal families joined forces through marriage.

examples.ko: 그 성은 오래전 왕가가 살던 곳이에요.
examples.en: That castle is where a royal family lived long ago.

explain: '왕실'과 비슷하게 쓰고, 역사 드라마나 박물관, 외국 왕실 소식에서 자주 들어요. 왕가에 속한 사람은 '왕족'이라고 해요. '왕가 출신', '왕가의 후손'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The whole royal family attended the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: '왕가'와 거의 같게 쓰고, 왕의 집안과 궁궐 쪽을 가리킬 때도 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used almost like '왕가', and often also points to the royal household and court.

phrases.en: That person is a descendant of old royalty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 왕가에 속한 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who belongs to a royal family.
phrases.en_equiv: royalty; member of the royal family

phrases.en: The main character of this drama comes from a royal family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 집안에서 태어났는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which family someone was born into.

explain_en: The ruling royal family of a kingdom. It is used much like '왕실' and is often heard in historical dramas, museums and news about foreign royalty. A person who belongs to a royal family is a '왕족'. Typical phrases are '왕가 출신' and '왕가의 후손'.

en: the bereaved; family of the deceased

examples.en: I offered words of comfort to the bereaved family.
The families of the accident victims held a press conference.
The bereaved family received mourners at the funeral hall.
The government decided to support the bereaved families.

examples.ko: 유가족의 슬픔은 말로 다 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The grief of the bereaved family cannot be put into words.

examples.ko: 그 병원에서는 유가족 상담을 해 줘요.
examples.en: That hospital offers counseling for bereaved families.

explain: 뉴스에서는 사고나 재난으로 숨진 사람의 가족을 가리킬 때 자주 나와요. 평소에 내 가족 이야기를 할 때는 쓰지 않고, 위로할 때는 '유가족분들께'처럼 높여 불러요.

phrases.en: I send my deepest condolences to the bereaved families.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위로하거나 뉴스에서 정중하게 부를 때 '-분들'을 붙여 높여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -분들 shows respect when offering comfort or speaking in the news.

phrases.en: Many people comforted the bereaved family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬픔에 빠진 가족에게 마음을 전할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when offering comfort to a grieving family.

phrases.en: A group to help the families of the victims was formed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고나 재난 뉴스에서 자주 붙어 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears together in news about accidents and disasters.

explain_en: In the news it often refers to the family of someone who died in an accident or disaster. You would not use it for your own family in daily talk, and when offering condolences you raise it politely, like '유가족분들께'.

examples.en: It's the weekend, so a lot of sightseers have gathered.
An announcement was made for the sightseers.
Sightseers have to buy tickets at the pier.

examples.ko: 호수에 유람객 몇 명이 배를 타고 있어요.
examples.en: A few sightseers are riding a boat on the lake.
The boat rocked, so the sightseers were startled.

examples.ko: 유람객의 안전을 위해 구명조끼를 입어야 해요.
examples.en: For the safety of sightseers, you must wear a life jacket.

explain: 일상에서는 '관광객'이 훨씬 일반적이고, '유람객'은 유람선이나 뱃놀이처럼 경치를 즐기는 장면에서 써요. 뉴스나 안내문에서 가끔 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Many tourists come in the summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 훨씬 일반적인 말이고, '유람객'은 경치를 즐기는 장면에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Far more common in daily use; '유람객' fits scenes of enjoying scenery.

phrases.en: The boat took the sightseers to the island.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유람선이나 배가 사람을 싣는 장면에서 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural in scenes where a boat takes people aboard.

phrases.en: Sightseers gathered to see the night view.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 한곳에 모이는 모습을 말할 때 '들'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '들' is added to show many people gathering in one place.

explain_en: In daily life '관광객' is far more general, while '유람객' is used in scenes of enjoying scenery, such as a cruise or boat ride. You may occasionally see it in news and notices.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 외국에서 온 이주자가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many migrants from abroad in this neighborhood.

examples.ko: 정부가 이주자를 위한 한국어 수업을 열었어요.
examples.en: The government opened Korean classes for migrants.
Migrants have a hard time finding a job at first.
I went to a group that helps migrant families.

examples.ko: 그분은 몇 년 전에 이 마을에 온 이주자예요.
examples.en: He is someone who moved to this village a few years ago.
We provide the information that migrants need.

explain: '이민자'는 주로 다른 나라로 옮겨 가 사는 사람을 말하고, '이주자'는 사는 곳을 옮긴 사람을 더 넓게 가리켜요. 뉴스나 공문서 같은 글에서 자주 보이고, 비슷한 말로 '이주민'도 있어요.

phrases.en: A new center that helps migrants has opened.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이주자'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화나 뉴스에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, a bit more common in daily talk and news.

phrases.en: The number of migrants in rural areas is growing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 지역으로 옮겨 오는 사람이 많아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when more people are moving into an area.

phrases.en: I got counseling at the migrant support center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공문서나 기관 이름에 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in official documents and organization names.

explain_en: '이민자' mainly refers to people who move to live in another country, while '이주자' covers people who have moved their place of residence more broadly. It is seen in writing such as news and official documents, and '이주민' is a similar word.

examples.en: The whole school gathered on the playground.

examples.ko: 전교생이 백 명도 안 되는 작은 학교예요.
examples.en: It is a small school with fewer than a hundred students in total.
The teacher greeted the entire student body.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 전교생이 같이 소풍을 가요.
examples.en: At this school all the students go on a picnic together.
I was nervous receiving an award in front of the whole school.
The singing of the whole school could be heard in the classroom.

explain: 전교생은 한 학교 전체 학생이에요. '전교'만 붙이면 학교 전체라는 범위가 되어서 '전교 일등'처럼 써요. 한 반이나 한 학년 전체는 '반 학생들', '학년 전체'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I gave a presentation in front of the entire school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 학생들이 모두 모인 자리에서 무언가 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when doing something where all the school's students are gathered.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the whole school

phrases.en: My older brother got first place in the whole school on the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전교'만 붙여 학교 전체에서의 순위를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses just 전교 to talk about rank within the entire school.

phrases.en: All the students in the school are going on a picnic.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모두'를 붙여 한 명도 빠지지 않는다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 모두 stresses that no student is left out.

explain_en: 전교생 means every student of one school. The part '전교' alone sets the range to the whole school, as in '전교 일등' (first in the school). One class or one grade is '반 학생들' or '학년 전체'.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 옛날에 온 정착민들이 세웠어요.
examples.en: This village was founded by settlers who came long ago.
The settlers and the native people held a festival together.

examples.ko: 새로 온 정착민에게 마을 사람들이 도움을 줬어요.
examples.en: The villagers helped the newly arrived settlers.
He is a descendant of the early settlers.
The settlers lived by farming at first.

examples.ko: 정착민 마을에는 아직 오래된 집이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Old houses still remain in the settlers' village.

explain: 다른 곳에서 옮겨 와 그 땅에 자리 잡고 사는 사람을 말해요. '이주민'은 옮겨 왔다는 점에, '정착민'은 자리를 잡고 살게 된 점에 초점이 있어요. 역사나 지리 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The early settlers built a village by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 땅에 처음 자리 잡은 사람들을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the people who first settled on the land.

phrases.en: The settlers and the native people shared their cultures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 살던 사람들과 비교할 때 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together when comparing with the people who lived there originally.

phrases.en: On festival days the settlers gather in the square.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 명을 가리킬 때 '-들'을 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-들' when referring to several settlers.

explain_en: It refers to people who moved from elsewhere and made a life on that land. '이주민' focuses on the fact that they moved, while '정착민' focuses on their having settled down. It often appears in history and geography topics.

examples.ko: 오전 아홉 시까지 운동장에 집결하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to gather on the field by nine in the morning.
Rescue workers are gathering at the scene of the accident.

examples.ko: 전국에서 모인 응원단이 경기장으로 집결하는 중이에요.
examples.en: Cheering squads from all over the country are converging on the stadium.

examples.ko: 사람들이 한곳에 집결하면 안전 문제가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If many people gather in one place, safety problems can arise.
We will set off after everyone has assembled.

examples.ko: 집결할 장소와 시간을 문자로 보내 주세요.
examples.en: Please text me the place and time to assemble.

explain: '모이다'는 아무 때나 쓰지만 집결하다는 많은 사람이 목적을 가지고 한곳에 모일 때 써요. 군대, 시위, 구조 같은 뉴스에서 자주 나오고 친구 모임에는 어색해요. '집합하다'는 정해진 시간에 모이라는 지시 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The assembly point is in front of the school gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '집결'을 명사로 써서 사람들이 모이기로 한 곳을 말해요. 안내문이나 공지에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form 집결 names the place people are to gather; common in notices and announcements.

phrases.en: The people who had been scattered gathered in one place.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한곳에'를 붙이면 여러 곳에 있던 사람들이 한 장소로 모인다는 느낌이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 한곳에 makes clear that people from various places came together at a single spot.

phrases.en: Police are assembled in front of the building.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 있다'를 붙여 이미 모여서 그 상태로 있다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -아/어 있다 it expresses the state of having already gathered and still being there.

explain_en: People or troops converge in one place, stiffer (운동장에 집결하다) 모이다 can be used any time, but 집결하다 is used when many people gather at one place for a purpose. It is common in news about the military, protests, or rescue, and sounds odd for a get-together of friends. 집합하다 has a feel of being told to gather at a set time.

t90.ax: We will set off after everyone has assembled.

examples.en: Who is known as the founder of taekwondo?
That person is the founder who created this school.

examples.ko: 이 학문의 창시자라고 불리는 사람을 알아요?
examples.en: Do you know the person called the founder of this field of study?

examples.ko: 창시자의 생각을 담은 책을 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm reading a book that contains the founder's ideas.

examples.ko: 그 운동의 창시자가 어제 강연을 했어요.
examples.en: The founder of that movement gave a lecture yesterday.
That recipe is a secret only the founder knows.

explain: '창시자'는 종교, 학문, 운동처럼 새로운 큰 흐름을 처음 연 사람에게 써요. 회사를 세운 사람은 '창업자', 물건을 처음 만든 사람은 '발명가'라고 해서 구별해요.

phrases.en: He is respected as the founder of this religion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로운 종교를 처음 연 사람을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the person who started a new religion.

phrases.example: 그는 이 운동의 창시자로 알려져 있어요.
phrases.en: He is known as the founder of this movement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실로 널리 알려진 내용을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for widely known facts.
phrases.en_equiv: to be known as the founder

phrases.example: 그 사람은 새 학문의 창시자가 됐어요.
phrases.en: That person became the founder of a new field of study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 흐름을 처음 시작한 사람이 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means becoming the person who first started a trend or field.

explain_en: First person to create a doctrine, martial art, or style. '창시자' is used for the person who first opened a new big current such as a religion, a field of study or a movement. For someone who set up a company people say '창업자', and for someone who first made a thing '발명가'.

t90.ax: Who is known as the founder of taekwondo?

examples.en: I went to the school during parent consultation week.
The parents gathered on the field and cheered for the children.
The teacher called the student's parent.
I gave the greeting as the parents' representative.

examples.ko: 학부형 중에는 학교 일을 도와주시는 분도 많아요.
examples.en: Among the parents, many help out with school events.

examples.ko: 오늘 학부형 모임이 오후 세 시에 있어요.
examples.en: The parents' meeting is today at three in the afternoon.

explain: 학교에 다니는 학생의 부모를 가리켜요. 같은 뜻으로 '학부모'도 쓰는데, '학부형'은 조금 예스럽게 들릴 수 있어요. 학생 본인에게는 쓰지 않고, 학교나 선생님 입장에서 부모를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: There is a parents' meeting at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 '학부형'보다 요즘 더 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but more common today than the headword.

phrases.en: There is a parent consultation next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선생님과 부모가 이야기하는 상담을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A consultation where the teacher talks with the parents.

phrases.en: The parents waited in front of the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 부모를 함께 가리킬 때 '들'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '들' to refer to several parents together.

explain_en: It refers to the parents of a student. '학부모' has the same meaning, but '학부형' can sound a little old-fashioned. It is not used for the student, and is used from the school's or teacher's viewpoint when talking about parents.

t90.ax: The teacher called the student's parent.

examples.ko: 미국에는 한인이 많이 사는 도시가 있어요.
examples.en: In the US there are cities where many Koreans live.
I bought kimchi at a Korean grocery store.
I went to an overseas Korean gathering for the first time.
They teach children Hangul at a Korean school.

examples.ko: 그곳 한인 사회는 서로 많이 도와요.
examples.en: The Korean community there helps one another a lot.
I went to a restaurant run by a Korean.

explain: 외국에 사는 한국 사람을 가리킬 때 주로 써요. '재미 한인', '한인 사회', '한인 마트'처럼 지역과 모임 이름에 붙어요. 한국 안에서 사는 한국 사람에게는 보통 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 그 도시의 한인 사회는 아주 커요.
phrases.en: That city's Korean community is very large.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국에 사는 한국 사람들의 모임이나 공동체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the group or community of Koreans living abroad.

phrases.en: I did the grocery shopping at a Korean mart on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국에서 한국 식품을 파는 가게를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a store abroad that sells Korean food.

phrases.example: 재미 한인 가수가 한국에서 콘서트를 해요.
phrases.en: A Korean American singer is holding a concert in Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재미'는 미국에 산다는 뜻이에요. 미국에 사는 한국 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '재미' means living in the U.S., so this refers to Koreans living in America.

explain_en: Mainly used for Koreans living abroad, as in '재미 한인' (Korean American), '한인 사회' (Korean community), '한인 마트'. It is not normally used for Koreans living in Korea.

en: to join forces; to combine forces

examples.ko: 친구들이 다 같이 합세해서 이삿짐을 날랐어요.
examples.en: My friends all pitched in together and carried the moving boxes.

examples.ko: 내가 이야기를 꺼내자 동생도 곧 합세했어요.
examples.en: When I brought it up, my younger sibling soon joined in too.

examples.ko: 합세한 두 회사가 새 서비스를 내놓았어요.
examples.en: The two companies that joined forces released a new service.

examples.ko: 이웃들도 청소에 합세하면 훨씬 빨리 끝날 거예요.
examples.en: If the neighbors join in the cleaning, it will be done much faster.
Even students from other classes gathered to join in.

examples.ko: 우리 편에 합세해 줘서 정말 고마워요.
examples.en: Thank you so much for joining our side.

explain: '-에 합세하다'처럼 이미 일을 하고 있거나 무리가 있는 곳에 뒤따라 끼어 힘을 보태는 느낌이에요. 그냥 모임에 들어올 때 쓰는 '합류하다'보다 '힘을 보탠다'는 느낌이 더 강해요. '힘을 합치다'는 처음부터 함께하는 경우에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My sister also joined in the cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-에 합세하다'처럼 이미 하고 있는 일에 끼어 힘을 보탤 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: As -에 합세하다, used when joining something already underway to help.

phrases.example: 다 같이 힘을 합치면 빨리 끝나요.
phrases.en: If we all join forces, it will finish quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음부터 함께 힘을 모을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used for pooling effort together from the start.

phrases.en: I joined my friends later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 보탠다기보다 모임이나 무리에 들어와 만난다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means joining up with a group rather than adding effort.

explain_en: People unite their efforts toward one goal (모두 합세하다) As in '-에 합세하다', it feels like following in to add your strength to a task or group that is already under way. It carries a stronger sense of 'lending your strength' than '합류하다', which just means joining a gathering. '힘을 합치다' can also be used when people work together from the start.
